items.q: The written vasoconstriction potency order is:
items.exp: Vasoconstriction potency: urotension > endothelin > AT-II. (Book p750)

items.q: The clinical feature and basic investigation picture of unilateral RAS are:
opts: Persistent HTN with RFT and urine analysis in the normal range
Persistent HTN with abnormal urine analysis
Flash pulmonary edema with raised S. creatinine
items.exp: C/F: persistent HTN; basic investigation (RFT, urine analysis) normal range. (Book p750)

items.q: In the affected kidney of unilateral RAS, the sequence after reduced RBF/perfusion is:
opts: Renin angiotensin system → ↑ aldosterone → ↑ AT-II → profound vasoconstriction → ↑ BP
items.exp: Affected kidney: ↓ RBF/perfusion → (+) renin angiotensin → (+) ↑ aldosterone → ↑ AT-II ↑↑ → profound vasoconstriction → ↑ BP → HTN/HTN crisis. (Book p750)

items.q: Fill up: In the normal kidney, ↑ renal interstitial hydrostatic pressure reduces reabsorption from the ______, producing pressure natriuresis.
items.exp: Normal kidney: ↑ RIHP → ↓ reabsorption from PCT → ↑ excretion of Na+/H2O (pressure natriuresis theory). (Book p750)

items.q: Which statement about the normal (contralateral) kidney in unilateral RAS is TRUE?
opts: It shows ↑ renal blood flow/medullary flow with ↑ RIHP
It shows ↓ renal blood flow and activated renin
It reabsorbs more sodium from the PCT
items.exp: Normal kidney: ↑ RBF/medullary flow → ↑ RIHP → ↓ PCT reabsorption → ↑ Na+/H2O excretion. (Book p750)

items.q: The book's note lists asymmetric kidney in vesicoureteral reflux and renal artery stenosis; it is NOT listed for:
items.exp: Asymmetric kidney seen in: vesicoureteral reflux; renal artery stenosis. (Book p750)

items.q: In the affected kidney, the doubly-raised AT-II produces:
opts: Profound vasoconstriction with rising blood pressure
items.exp: ↑ Angiotensin II (AT-II) ↑↑ → profound vasoconstriction → ↑ blood pressure → HTN/HTN crisis. (Book p750)
